title: Reduced structure unit kills the pulled-back supporting kernel
statement: Let X, Z, S and Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme], k:Z -> X a closed immersion with ideal J=ker(k) [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], j:S -> X any morphism, and p:Y -> S finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let G be a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] killed by J on every open, and let psi:j^*G ~= p_*O_Y be an O_S-module isomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write q:O_X -> k_*O_Z for the canonical structure map and epsilon_j:j^*O_X -> O_S for the canonical pullback structure unit [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Then j^*(kernel(q) -> O_X), followed by epsilon_j and the structure map O_S -> p_*O_Y, is zero. No compatibility system, Noetherian base, completeness, multiplication on G or global unit in G is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09ZT, algebra structure paragraph, expanded local unit factorization using Modules Tags 01BG and 0096 and the closed-immersion quotient; official pages read 2026-10-13.

proof.text: The kernel K of the closed-immersion structure map is quasi-coherent: both the structure unit and its closed-immersion pushforward are quasi-coherent, and kernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent. On an affine V, the kernel condition shows that the kernel inclusion sends K(V) into ker(k.app V), which is k.ker.ideal V. The all-open idealOfOpens agrees with this affine ideal, so hkill annihilates G(V) by these scalars. No quotient identification or ideal product is needed.

On affine V in X and U in S contained in j inverse V, use exists_tensorPullback_affine_sections for K, G, and the unit. The characterization of tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit by the adjunction unit, together with restriction naturality, gives epsilon(c_unit(a tensor b)) = b times j.appLE(a). Naturality of the affine comparison identifies the pulled-back kernel inclusion on pure tensors. A scalar from x tensor b therefore acts on the pullback of G as b times the image of the original scalar i(x). A-linearity of the section comparison and tensor induction reduce this action to i(x) acting on a section of G(V), which is zero by hkill. Additivity and tensor induction in K give annihilation by every scalar in the image.

Paired affine opens form a basis: first choose an affine neighbourhood V of j(x), then an affine U inside the given open intersected with j inverse V. Apply sheaf separatedness to the section a times t of j-star G. Restriction compatibility of scalar multiplication and naturality of the pulled-back kernel composite identify its restrictions with the affine annihilation calculation. This proves annihilation on all opens.

For each open U and section s of j-star K, let a be its image in O_S(U). Apply the proved scalar annihilation to psi inverse of the section 1 of p-star O_Y. Apply psi hom and use its O_S-linearity and inverse identity to obtain a times 1 = 0 in p-star O_Y. Its scalar action is multiplication by p.app U applied to a, so multiplication by 1 yields p.app U(a) = 0. Module morphism extensionality gives the requested composite equation. Empty opens and zero algebras use exactly the same identities.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteStructure_supported_unit_kernel_zero
    {X Z S Y : Scheme.{u}} (k : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion k]
    (j : S ⟶ X) (p : Y ⟶ S) [IsFinite p]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hkill : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, U)), a ∈ k.ker.idealOfOpens U →
      ∀ s : Γ(G, U), a • s = 0)
    (ψ : (tensorPullback j).obj G ≅
      (pushforward p).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf)) :
    (tensorPullback j).map
        (CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.ι
          (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit k.toRingCatSheafHom)) ≫
      tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit j ≫
        SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit p.toRingCatSheafHom = 0
